name: Converging Plate-Loaded Chest Press
description: The Converging Plate-Loaded Chest Press uses an independent-arm machine where each handle moves in a converging arc (the arms come together as they extend forward), mimicking the natural adduction component of the pectoral contraction. The plate-loaded design allows greater load than selectorized machines and the converging motion provides superior pectoral peak contraction.

execution.starting_position: Load the machine with weight plates. Sit with back against the pad and grip the handles at chest level.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the seat height so handles align with the mid-chest. Load plates evenly on each side. Use the starting pin to bring handles to the starting position if provided.
steps: Step 1: Grip both handles and press forward, allowing the arms to naturally converge toward the midline.
Step 2: Fully extend the arms and squeeze the chest as the handles come together.
Step 3: Return under control, allowing the arms to diverge back to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat without letting the weight stack touch at the bottom.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you press and handles converge. Inhale as you return.
common_mistakes: Letting the weight stack slam at the bottom
Not squeezing the chest at peak contraction when arms converge
safety_considerations: Load plates evenly — imbalanced loading creates asymmetric movement
Use the starting pin to control the entry and exit safely under heavy loads
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension and convergence at front; return to full stretch of pectorals at back.
coaching_cues: Let the arms come together at the top — squeeze the pecs hard
Control the return — feel the stretch
